analysis:
The only change in this PR is a test-only addition at MediaIngestTests.swift head lines 234-251, a new test `vlmDecodeVideoLabelAliases`. It checks that decodeVideo admits the MIME label aliases video/mov, video/x-m4v and VIDEO/MOV for base64 data: URIs, and that the bytes still decide acceptance. Non-video bytes labelled video/mov must throw malformedDataURI. A non-base64 data:video/mov URI must also throw malformedDataURI. The rest of the file is unchanged. The base and head units at 673+ and 675+ differ only by the 19-line offset from the inserted test.

I saw no production source in this batch. The test implies a MediaIngest.swift change that widens the accepted video MIME labels, but that file is not supplied. A wider label allowlist could affect TB-003 or TB-007 media handling, which covers the SSRF and local-file-read guard, the in-memory-only video policy (T-050) and the decoded-byte caps. The existing tests in the same file still pin the key guarantees. Non-data: http(s) and file URIs are rejected with invalidURL (lines 132-144, 343-355). Video stays memory-backed with no temp file (lines 196-221). Unknown containers such as webm are rejected (lines 327-341). Byte, frame-pixel and count caps are tested (lines 763-834). The new test also checks that a non-video payload with an alias label fails closed, and that the percent-encoded alias form is rejected. No security regression is evident from the test change itself.

Remaining question for integration: confirm in the MediaIngest.swift source that alias handling is case-insensitive, still requires base64 for video, still applies the byte cap before AVAsset construction, and still has no disk fallback. That source was not provided, so I cannot verify it here.
